facts.statement: Bryantolepis lived during the Early Devonian period.
Bryantolepis lived between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species Bryantolepis brachycephala was described by Bryant in 1932.
facts.quote: The type species Bryantolepis brachycephala was described by Bryant in 1932

facts.statement: Bryantolepis brachycephala was originally classified in the genus Euryaspis before being reassigned to Bryantolepis.
facts.quote: It was originally placed in the genus Euryaspis, but was later reassigned to Bryantolepis

facts.statement: The species Bryantolepis williamsi was described and named in 2010.
facts.quote: The second species, Bryantolepis williamsi, was described and named in 2010

facts.statement: The species name williamsi honors the paleontologist Michael E. Williams.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, williamsi, honors paleontologist Michael E. Williams (1940-2003)

facts.statement: Bryantolepis brachycephala is one of the most common fish species found in the Beartooth Butte Formation.
facts.quote: It is one of the most common fishes found at the Beartooth Butte Formation

facts.statement: Bryantolepis williamsi was found at the Utah-Idaho border in the Grassy Flat Member of the Water Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: It was found at the Utah-Idaho border, specifically in the Grassy Flat Member of the Water Canyon Formation, Green Canyon, northern Utah, and St. Charles, southern Idaho

facts.statement: Fossils of Bryantolepis include parts of the skull roof, suborbital region, endocranium, and trunk shield.
facts.quote: The genus is known from multiple parts of the skull roof, the suborbital, endocranium, and trunk shield

facts.statement: Bryantolepis belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Bryantolepis is classified in the class Placodermi.
